spec.name: Earnings drift v19
spec.notes: Post-earnings drift on the reported surprise.

claim.text: Research-period backtest: Sharpe 1.9, annual return 7%, maximum drawdown 4%.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.91 to 1.23 (change -0.68).
Under strict point-in-time data the Sharpe ratio moves from 1.91 to 1.91. Strict mode changed no field or operator the signal uses.
At 10 bps the Sharpe ratio is 1.88 (as submitted, 8 bps: 1.91); it breaks even at 135.3 bps with daily turnover 0.02.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 1.91 against 1.91 as submitted; the strategy never saw 0 delisted assets.
On the sealed period (strict mode, 10 bps) the Sharpe ratio is 1.06 against 1.91 in research, a gap of +0.84.
The best year gives 19% of total P&L (year 8) and calm regimes give 71%; Sharpe is 2.23 in calm and 1.62 in stressed regimes.
The log holds 4 distinct specs; the best of 4 under no edge is expected to reach a Sharpe of 0.26, so the claimed 1.90 becomes 1.64 and the probability that the true Sharpe is above zero is 100%.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 2.02 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.04, 95th percentile 0.64).
Perturbing the 3 numeric values in the signal by up to 50% moves the Sharpe ratio from 1.91 to as low as 1.55 (as low as 1.68 at 25%).
The top 1% of days (22 days) give 34% of total P&L and the top 5 assets give 18% (net of the strategy's own costs).

series.label: cumulative share of P&L, best days first
